To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the creation of the regulatory body in Brazil was a biased process, in which the technocratic model of risk assessment was adopted to guarantee the legitimacy of a decision-making process that aligned with the interests of the technology providers.
the Brazilian regulatory system is not sustainable because it does not guarantee public participation, transparency and the independence of the regulatory body.
the Brazilian regulatory system for GMOs is a technocratic model, which is not aligned with democratic principles and is biased in favour of the interests of technology providers.

the issues concerning the sustainability of a regulatory body that is supposed to be a central piece of the regulatory policies governing GMOs in Brazil.

the following issues: (1) the role of the Brazilian Biosafety Commission (COB) in the regulation of genetically modified organisms (2) the role of COB in the decision-making process (3) the role of civil society in the decision-making processes and (4) the role of public participation in the decision-making.
the following questions: What are the issues concerning the creation of a sustainable regulatory body for GMOs in the Brazilian case?

the Brazilian regulatory system is not sustainable.
the Brazilian regulatory body is a model of regulatory capture.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a regulatory body for GMOs in Brazilian agriculture should be established as an independent agency.

the regulatory body created by the Brazilian government to deal with the issue of GMOs is not sustainable, in the sense that it is unable to provide the necessary legitimacy for the decision-making process, as it does not allow for the inclusion of the interests of the society in the process.
the Brazilian model of regulation of GMOs is a clear example of the technocratic model of risk governance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite of the fact that Brazil has a strong institutional framework for regulating GMOs, the process of risk assessment and management of these organisms in the Brazilian context does not guarantee a sustainable model of decision-making.

the Brazilian experience in regulating GMOs is an important lesson for other countries, especially those in the developing world, in terms of the risks associated with the creation of regulatory bodies with no democratic legitimacy.
the current model of regulation of GMOs is unsustainable and needs to be changed.
